Here’s a highly advanced Keras + Spektral project leveraging graph neural networks for multivariate time-series forecasting on spatial-temporal graphs—a big leap from previous work.

🧠 Project Title

ai-ml-ds-xYwZa8GhTkM: Spatial‑Temporal Forecasting with Graph Neural Networks
Filename: spatial_temporal_gnn_forecasting.py

Short Description:
A Spektral-based Keras model that extends T‑GCN and StemGNN principles: it embeds a dynamic graph structure (e.g., sensor network), models temporal dependencies via GRU, and leverages GCN for spatial graph convolution. Forecasts future time steps across all nodes concurrently.

# spatial_temporal_gnn_forecasting.py

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import networkx as nx
from sklearn.preprocessing import MinMaxScaler
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras import Model, Input
from tensorflow.keras.layers import GRU, Dense, Dropout, TimeDistributed
from spektral.layers import GCNConv
from spektral.data import Dataset, Graph
from spektral.data.loaders import DisjointLoader

# Generate synthetic spatio-temporal dataset
class STDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, n_nodes: int=10, T: int=200, **kwargs):
        self.n_nodes: int = n_nodes
        self.T: int = T
        super().__init__(**kwargs)

    def read(self):
        t: np.ndarray = np.arange(self.T)
        data: np.ndarray = np.sin(0.1 * t)[None, :] * np.linspace(0.5, 2, self.n_nodes)[:, None]
        data += 0.1 * np.random.randn(self.n_nodes, self.T)
        scaler = MinMaxScaler(feature_range=(0, 1))
        data = scaler.fit_transform(data)
        graphs: list[Graph] = []
        G = nx.circular_ladder_graph(self.n_nodes // 2)
        a = nx.adjacency_matrix(G)
        for i in range(self.T - 10):
            x: np.ndarray = data[:, i:i+10].T  # shape (10, n_nodes)
            y: np.ndarray = data[:, i+10]      # shape (n_nodes,)
            graphs.append(Graph(x=x, a=a, y=y))
        return graphs

# Build dataset and loader
dataset: STDataset = STDataset()
loader = DisjointLoader(dataset, batch_size=32, epochs=100)

# Build the model: spatial-temporal GNN
n_nodes: int = dataset.n_nodes
timesteps: int = 10
features: int = 1

x_in = Input(shape=(timesteps, n_nodes, features))
a_in = Input(shape=(None, None), sparse=True)
x = TimeDistributed(GCNConv(16, activation='relu'))([x_in, a_in])
x = TimeDistributed(Dropout(0.3))(x)
x = tf.reshape(x, (-1, timesteps, n_nodes * 16))
x = GRU(64, activation='tanh')(x)
x = Dense(n_nodes)(x)
model = Model(inputs=[x_in, a_in], outputs=x)
model.compile('adam', loss='mse', metrics=['mae'])

# Train
model.fit(loader.load(), steps_per_epoch=loader.steps_per_epoch, epochs=20)

# Forecast function
def forecast(model: Model, seq: np.ndarray, adj: tf.SparseTensor) -> np.ndarray:
    inp_x: np.ndarray = seq[..., None]
    return model.predict([inp_x, adj])[0]

🚀 Key Learnings

  • Frameworks: TensorFlow 2.x, Keras API, Spektral (GNN)
  • Concepts: Spatial → GCN, Temporal → GRU, Dynamic graph-time-series interplay
  • Keywords: T-GCN, StemGNN, ST-GNN, spectral convolution, disjoint graph loader
  • Research Areas: Graph representation learning, spatio-temporal forecasting, sensor networks
  • Hashtags/Googleables: #SpatialTemporalNN, #GraphTimeSeries, #Spektral, #SpektralGCN, #STGNN

🏭 Problem Domain

Multivariate spatio-temporal forecasting in graph contexts—sensor networks, traffic, IoT, and epidemiology modeling.

Use Cases

  • Predict next-day traffic volume per sensor
  • Environmental forecasting (air quality, weather sensors)
  • Predictive maintenance in manufacturing networks

🧱 Frameworks Used

  • TensorFlow 2.x + Keras
  • Spektral for GCN layers
  • NetworkX, NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn

🗂 Development Lifecycle

  1. Requirements Gathering: Define forecasting horizon, node/network structure.
  2. Data Pipeline: Streaming sensor data → preprocessing → graph construction.
  3. Feature Engineering: Scaling, normalization, sequence windowing.
  4. Model Design: Spatial-temporal GCN+GRU architecture.
  5. Training: Disjoint batching, early stopping, checkpointing.
  6. Testing: Simulated and real-world validation.
  7. Deployment: TensorFlow Serving or Edge inference.
  8. Monitoring: On-model drift, real-time retraining triggers.
  9. Maintenance: Continual learning, hyperparameter tuning schedule.

🤝 Sister Projects

  • Anomaly Detection: Detect unexpected deviations in future forecasts
  • Graph Autoencoder: Learn dynamic embeddings of node signals
  • Spatio-temporal Attention GNN: Incorporate Transformers for longer sequence forecasting

🔗 Integration Opportunities

  • Edge devices: Real-time forecasting on IoT hardware
  • Time-Series APIs: Integration with InfluxDB / OpenTSDB
  • Dashboards: Predictive visualization in Grafana

⏱ Timestamp

2025-07-15

⏱ Timeframe

~4–6 weeks end-to-end, including integration and deployment.

🎯 Final Product Output

  • A forecasting service/API that ingests the latest window of time-series data and outputs future time steps per node in real time.
  • Backed by GCN+GRU pipeline, scalable to edge/cloud deployment.

💡 Bonus Challenge

Add attention pooling: integrate a self-attention layer post-GRU to focus predictions dynamically on key nodes. Or incorporate adaptive adjacency learning, allowing the network to learn evolving graph connectivity as time progresses.

🔭 Where to Go Next

  • Scale to real-world datasets (e.g., METR-LA traffic, PEMS)
  • Add probabilistic forecasting with quantile regression
  • Upgrade to Transformer‑GNN hybrids for deeper spatio‑temporal pattern modeling
  • Optimize for Edge AI deployment using TensorFlow Lite

This project integrates advanced graph and temporal modeling to produce powerful, production-ready forecasting systems—well above standard sequence or CNN tasks.
